analysis.title: Data Center Capacity Model: ~20% CAGR to Over 300 GW by 2030E; EQIX Top Pick
key_insights: MS base case sees global data center IT capacity rising from 136 GW in 2026E to 316 GW by 2030E, a 23% CAGR, adding about 180 GW. Bull case is 377 GW (28% CAGR) and bear case is 240 GW.

MS forecasts a 49 GW (Utility) global power shortfall by 2028E: 327 GW of demand against 278 GW of supply. The shortfall is 3 GW in 2026E. The conversion from IT to Utility GW assumes PUE of 1.27 in 2026E and 1.24 in 2028E.

The US shortfall is 43 GW (Utility) by 2028E (180 GW demand vs 137 GW supply), up from 15 GW in 2026E. US IT capacity grows from 65 GW in 2026E to 152 GW in 2030E, a 24% CAGR. US bull case is 177 GW and bear case is 131 GW.

MS names Equinix (EQIX) its Top Pick in Communications Infrastructure. Reasons given: diversified enterprise base, interconnection network, and achievable Street estimates. Supply constraints are expected to add value to scaled operators with access to power.

MS expects colocation operators (EQIX, CSQR, DLR) to perform well because cost inflation, moratoriums and permitting delays strengthen pricing power. Smaller colocation facilities face less community opposition than large AI campuses.

Top 10 operators' owned IT capacity grows from 43.1 GW in 2026E to 139.0 GW in 2030E, a 34% CAGR. Alphabet grows to 33.9 GW (49% CAGR) and SpaceX (Terrestrial) to 22.8 GW (72% CAGR). Amazon reaches 22.5 GW, Microsoft 18.7 GW, Meta 15.8 GW.

Alphabet is forecast to lead 2030E global IT capacity share at about 9%, up from about 5% in 2026. SpaceX (Terrestrial) is second at 6%, with Amazon at 6% and Microsoft at 5%. Owners/Developers (EQIX, DLR) give up about 3 percentage points of share by 2030.
Clouds gain the most share from 2026 to 2030, followed by power-secured providers (PSPs such as WULF and CIFR) and neoclouds, all taking share from the long tail of compute owners.

AlphaWise survey: average price of data center capacity contracts signed in the last 3 months is up 11% y/y, with 56% of respondents seeing increases above 10%. Respondents have 43% of capacity pre-leased on average, and expect customer demand for future capacity to rise 20% on average by 2030.

MS 3Q26 CIO survey: about 45% of companies use open-weight AI models today, expected to roughly double to about 90% in three years. Open-weight models run 8% of workloads today, expected at 19%. MS sees this as a tailwind for colocation operators, particularly EQIX, because enterprises deploy private models in colocation facilities.

EQIX 3Q26 preview (earnings 10/28): MS expects 10.6% y/y total revenue growth, 10.4% growth in both colocation and interconnection, and $480mn bookings. MS capex yield analysis shows upside to recurring revenue estimates through 2029E. Rating Overweight, PT $1,250 (25.0x EV/'28 EBITDA).

DLR: Equal-weight, PT $215 (20.5x EV/'28 EBITDA). MS notes about 5% dilution from 15.6mn shares/OP units issued to fund capacity expansion, and expects renewal spreads to surprise upward again after +25% in 2Q26. DLR reports 10/29 after the close. MS says EQIX's 10/28 results will be a read-through to DLR's 0-1 MW bookings.

CSQR: Overweight, PT $26 with about 80% upside, from a $14.34 price. MS expects 14 MW to become sellable this quarter and models about $640mn of growth capex in 2026. The multiple could re-rate from 12.6x EV/'27 EBITDA if Csquare eases market worries about execution and deleveraging.

BXDC: Equal-weight, PT $23. The market is cautious on rising rates and a 1% management fee payable to Blackstone starting mid-November. A lower share price raises BXDC's cost of capital and narrows potential acquisition spreads.

MS bottom-up method applies historical probabilities of a data center project moving from under construction to in-service capacity, with haircuts to future probabilities for rising delay risk. It is combined with a top-down view by territory.

market_movers.rationale: Named Top Pick in Communications Infrastructure on interconnection scale, diversified enterprise base and power-constrained supply. Bull $1,500 and bear $850 cases given.
Market is seen as overly optimistic about near-term AI-driven growth. Exposure to wholesale leasing gives longer leases and lower pricing per kW.
About 80% upside to PT. A re-rating depends on capacity delivery, interconnection growth and deleveraging.
Blind-pool execution risk and a 1% management fee starting mid-November weigh on the shares. MS is waiting for an accretive acquisition.

sector_views.rationale: MS industry view is In-Line. Within it, colocation data center operators with secured power are favored because supply constraints support pricing.

earnings_insights: EQIX 3Q26 (reports 10/28), MS estimates, not yet reported: total revenue growth 10.6% y/y, colocation and interconnection revenue growth 10.4% each, bookings $480mn.
EQIX FY26E MS estimates: revenue growth about 11.6%, adjusted EBITDA margin 51%, AFFO per share growth about 12.6%. MS FY26E FFO per share is $42.99 vs consensus mean $43.17.

DLR (reports 10/29 after the close): MS expects renewal spreads to surprise upward again, after +25% in 2Q26 (reported). FY26E MS estimate: revenue growth about 16.3%, adjusted EBITDA margin 54.0%, AFFO per share growth about 17.9%.

CSQR 3Q26: MS expects 14 MW to turn into sellable capacity this quarter. FY26E MS revenue growth is 17.1% and adjusted EBITDA growth is 21.1%. MS FY26E FFO per share is $0.59 vs consensus $0.98 (as printed in the table), and EPS is -$1.85 vs consensus -$1.71.
BXDC FY26E MS estimates: AFFO per share $0.37, NOI ramping to about $20mn in 2026E and about $275mn in 2027E.
crypto_views: Power-secured providers (PSPs), a group MS lists as including Applied Digital, Cipher Mining, Galaxy Digital, Hut8, IREN, MARA, RIOT and TeraWulf, are forecast to take data center capacity share from 2026 to 2030. Hut8, Galaxy Digital and Applied Digital are among the largest owned-capacity adders (about 3 GW each, 2026E-2030E).

trade_ideas.description: Overweight EQIX ahead of 10/28 earnings, PT $1,250, as Top Pick in Communications Infrastructure
trade_ideas.rationale: Supply constraints give value to scaled operators with access to power, and capex yield analysis shows upside to Street revenue estimates.
trade_ideas.risk: Macro softness reducing IT infrastructure investment, excess supply pressuring pricing, larger power density requirements raising obsolescence risk, and interest rates staying higher for longer.

trade_ideas.rationale: Brownfield expansion yields and constrained power supply support pricing, with a re-rating possible if deleveraging is delivered.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher labor and construction costs pressure development yields, macro softness, and higher interest rates.

risk_factors: Macroeconomic softness reducing IT data center investment.
Excess supply coming online and pressuring pricing power.
Larger than expected power density requirements increasing obsolescence risk of current facilities.
Interest rates staying higher for longer, weighing on data center REIT multiples.
Execution and leverage risk at CSQR, and blind-pool execution risk at BXDC.
The role of inference in colocation data centers remains uncertain, and hyperscalers continue to build their own AI data centers.
Higher labor and construction costs for development.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows global data center capacity of 54 GW in 2022 rising to 108 GW in 2025, 136 GW in 2026E and 316 GW in 2030E.
Exhibit 2 shows the global shortfall growing from 3 GW (Utility) in 2026E to 49 GW in 2028E, with supply of 173 GW rising to 278 GW.
Exhibit 5 shows the base, bull (377 GW) and bear (240 GW) capacity scenarios to 2030E.
Exhibit 28 shows companies using open-weight models rising from 46% today to 87% in three years, and workload share from 8% to 19%.
vol_and_positioning: EQIX options-implied probabilities as of 23 Oct 2026: about 4.9% chance of exceeding $1,500, about 18.4% of exceeding $1,250, and about 32.5% of falling below $850 over 12 months.
Hedge fund sector long/short ratio is 1.4x with 1.9% net exposure for EQIX and DLR. EQIX institutional ownership is 53.1% active.
MS notes EQIX at $955.03, DLR at $174.53, CSQR at $14.34 and BXDC at $16.17 as of 10/26/2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Power supply constraints, with a 49 GW global shortfall by 2028E and contract pricing up 11%, support pricing for operators with secured power, and colocation is insulated from community opposition.
tension_points.bear_case: Excess supply coming online could pressure pricing, and the role of inference in colocation data centers remains uncertain as hyperscalers build their own AI campuses.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Macro softness reducing IT infrastructure investment, with absorption and presales falling short of expectations (EQIX bear case $850).

theme_stances.key_argument: Compute demand is likely to exceed supply for years, creating a 49 GW (Utility) global shortfall by 2028E that benefits time-to-power providers.
theme_stances.evidence: demand for compute is likely to significantly exceed supply for years to come

theme_stances.key_argument: Cost inflation, moratoriums and permitting delays should strengthen pricing power for colocation operators.
Enterprise adoption of open-weight models should pull workloads to colocation data centers, which benefits EQIX in particular.
theme_stances.evidence: we see open-weight share gains as a positive for colocation operators
